sections.title: Syllable Count and Stem Rules
sections.content: Hungarian forms causative verbs ('to have something done' or 'to make someone do something') by attaching -at/-et or -tat/-tet to the verb stem before tense and person endings. As a core morphological rule, most monosyllabic stems take -at/-et (ír -> írat 'has written', kér -> kéret 'has summoned', mos -> mosat 'has washed', fest -> festet 'has painted'), whereas polysyllabic stems and monosyllabic stems ending in vowel + -t take -tat/-tet (olvas -> olvastat 'makes read', javít -> javíttat 'has repaired/corrected', épít -> építtet 'has built', fut -> futtat 'makes run').

sections.title: Consonant Clusters and Irregular Stems
sections.content: Even among monosyllabic verbs, stems ending in certain consonant clusters or specific lexical roots prefer -tat/-tet to preserve clarity (e.g. küld -> küldet or küldözget, but jár -> járat 'runs a service / makes walk', hív -> hívat 'summons'). Notice that vowel harmony strictly governs the suffix vowel: back stems select -at/-tat (másol -> másoltat, vár -> várat), while front stems select -et/-tet (ellenőriz -> ellenőriztet, keres -> kerestet).

sections.title: Monosyllabic (-at/-et) vs. Polysyllabic (-tat/-tet) Causatives
rows: A professzor esszét írat a hallgatókkal. (The professor has the students write an essay.)
Az igazgató az irodájába kérette a diákot. (The principal had the student summoned to his office.)
Sok eredeti forrást olvastat velünk. (She makes us read many original sources.)
Kijavíttatta a sajtóhibákat a kéziratban. (He had the typographical errors corrected in the manuscript.)

items.spanish: A tanszékvezető minden félévben új szakirodalmat fordíttat a doktoranduszokkal.
items.english: The department chair has the doctoral students translate new academic literature every semester.

items.spanish: A szerkesztő alaposan átvizsgáltatta a szöveget a nyomdába küldés előtt.
items.english: The editor had the text thoroughly examined before sending it to the printing press.

items.spanish: Miért váratod a bizottság tagjait a folyosón?
items.english: Why are you keeping the committee members waiting in the corridor?

items.spanish: A könyvtáros ritka kéziratokat másoltatott a kutatóintézet számára.
items.english: The librarian had rare manuscripts copied for the research institute.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: Watch the double -tt- in verbs ending in -ít: 'javít' ('corrects') becomes 'javíttat' ('has corrected') in the present and 'javíttatott' ('had corrected') in the past!
